output.myth: Tiru went out in a boat with the red sail when the Gale was young, and Tavo took the boat and did not give it back. His mother climbed to the cliff each night and flew his red kite into the wind, so that a lamp would show to the boats still out. Hesk counts the string, and she counted it every night. Nobody told her to stop. One evening Tavo came back laughing, and the wind pulled the kite from her hands and it went up past the Gulls into Vel. It did not come down. Now the red lamp hangs low over the Leeward Reach, and the sailors say you can see it burn on nights when a boat is still out. If you see it, do not wave. Tiru is in the boat. Keep your own lamp lit and come home by it.

guess: A kite with cross-spars, a bow-tie tail and a string curving off to the right
